name: 2one DLS knowledge graph
description: Semantic decision graph for the 2one Design System. Two layers: derived (parsed from source) and authored (graph/decisions.json — intents, rules, preferences). Nodes carry an ontology class + provenance; edges carry provenance + decision priority. Reason over it with scripts/graph-decide.mjs. Generated by scripts/build-graph.mjs.

nodes.label: Accessible label
nodes.description: Inputs and controls must have a programmatic label.

nodes.label: APCA + WCAG contrast
nodes.description: Text/UI pairs must clear their APCA Lc threshold, audited light and dark.

nodes.label: Focus management
nodes.description: Overlays must trap and restore focus.

nodes.label: Keyboard operable
nodes.description: All interactive controls must be reachable and operable by keyboard.

nodes.label: Never signal state by colour alone
nodes.description: State must carry an icon, label, or shape in addition to colour.

nodes.label: Reduced-motion support
nodes.description: Animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Scrim behind text over media
nodes.description: Never place text directly over media — lay a scrim behind it.

nodes.label: Visible focus indicator
nodes.description: A focusable control must show a focus ring (Lc 15 non-text floor).

nodes.label: Guardrail notice
nodes.description: A refusal in its own (grayscale) shape, offering the nearest safe alternative. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Loading state
nodes.description: A pixel matrix + Skeleton holding the frame before the first token. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Reasoning effort
nodes.description: Effort level (label + segment shape) and budget spent vs allotted. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Reasoning panel
nodes.description: A collapsible timeline of reasoning steps that settles into a summary. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Streaming text
nodes.description: Answer tokens revealed over time; the leading edge carries the brand accent, then settles to ink. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Thinking indicator
nodes.description: A live status line naming the current step, with elapsed time. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Typing indicator
nodes.description: Three grayscale dots signalling the assistant is composing. Reasoning category.

nodes.label: Mission
nodes.value: To create structure in an unstructured world.

nodes.label: Confirmation flow
nodes.description: A step that gates an action behind explicit confirmation.

nodes.label: Desktop / md+
nodes.description: Viewport at the md breakpoint and above.

nodes.label: Mobile
nodes.description: Below md; useIsMobile() is true.

nodes.label: Web
nodes.description: Any browser context.

nodes.label: Action toolbar
nodes.description: A row of controls where a critical action must stay reachable.

nodes.label: App shell
nodes.description: The top-level product frame — brand, navigation, and a content region.

nodes.label: Authenticate
nodes.description: Sign in or sign up.

nodes.label: Chart
nodes.description: A chart or data visualisation.

nodes.label: Confirm an action
nodes.description: Ask the user to confirm before proceeding.

nodes.label: Dashboard
nodes.description: An overview dashboard: KPI tiles, a data table and charts.

nodes.label: Data table
nodes.description: A sortable, selectable table of records.

nodes.label: Destructive action
nodes.description: An action that deletes or irreversibly changes data.

nodes.label: Convey essential information
nodes.description: Information the user MUST perceive to succeed (required, error, or instruction).

nodes.label: Hold the frame before first output
nodes.description: Keep the frame while the model has nothing to show yet.

nodes.label: Login
nodes.description: A sign-in screen.

nodes.label: Low-emphasis action
nodes.description: A secondary/tertiary action that must not compete with the primary.

nodes.label: Show a media placeholder
nodes.description: An on-brand stand-in where an image or video will go but none is loaded.

nodes.label: Navigate
nodes.description: Move between views or destinations.

nodes.label: Post to a feed
nodes.description: Show one item in a social/activity feed — author, body, optional media, low-emphasis reactions.

nodes.label: Present pricing
nodes.description: Explain plans and convert a visitor to a paid plan.

nodes.label: Primary action
nodes.description: The single most important action in a view or section.

nodes.label: Recover from an error
nodes.description: Understand and fix an invalid input.

nodes.label: Refuse with a safe alternative
nodes.description: Decline a request and offer the nearest thing the agent can do instead.

nodes.label: Report reasoning effort
nodes.description: Show how hard to think and how much of that budget was spent.

nodes.label: Select an option
nodes.description: Choose one or more values from a set.

nodes.label: Show a comment thread
nodes.description: Show a thread of comments and let the reader add one.

nodes.label: Show a media gallery
nodes.description: Show a set of images/videos as a browsable grid or carousel, with a lightbox.

nodes.label: Show a profile
nodes.description: Introduce a person/account at the top of a profile — avatar, name, bio, stats, one primary relationship action.

nodes.label: Show the reasoning trace
nodes.description: Reveal the model's intermediate steps without dominating the answer.

nodes.label: Show a side panel
nodes.description: A secondary panel beside the main content — inline on desktop, a Sheet on mobile.

nodes.label: Signal the agent is composing
nodes.description: Lightweight presence cue that a reply is coming, with no named step.

nodes.label: Signal the agent is working
nodes.description: Tell the user the agent is working right now, and on what.

nodes.label: Signup
nodes.description: A create-account screen.

nodes.label: Stat tiles / KPIs
nodes.description: A row of KPI / metric tiles.

nodes.label: Stream an answer
nodes.description: Show an assistant answer as its tokens arrive.

nodes.label: Submit a form
nodes.description: Send the data the user has entered.

nodes.label: Show supplementary info
nodes.description: Reveal optional, non-essential helper information.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.description: Sign-in / sign-up composed from Card + Label + Input + Button.

nodes.label: Comment thread
nodes.description: A list of comment Items (Avatar + body) plus a single Textarea composer with one primary Post button.

nodes.label: Destructive confirmation
nodes.description: AlertDialog gating a destructive action, confirmed by a destructive button.

nodes.label: Feed item
nodes.description: One feed post: a Card with an author Item (Avatar), body, optional media placeholder, and a row of ghost reaction Buttons. No primary — reactions are low-emphasis.

nodes.label: Form submission
nodes.description: Label + Input + validation message, one primary submit.

nodes.label: Media gallery
nodes.description: Media as a grid/Carousel of Cards with a Dialog lightbox; Empty when there are none. Text over media sits on a scrim.

nodes.label: Mobile side panel
nodes.description: A panel that renders inline on md+ and as a Sheet on mobile.

nodes.label: Pricing page
nodes.description: Complete pricing-page composition: plans (Card + billing toggle + recommended) then comparison Table, FAQ and CTA. One primary action; included/excluded shown by icon + text.

nodes.label: Profile header
nodes.description: Profile top: large Avatar, name/handle, bio, a stats row, and exactly one primary relationship Button (Follow / Edit).

nodes.label: A draft is delivered in both themes
nodes.statement: Every screen in a draft is rendered and reviewed in light AND dark. Dark is not invert-and-ship: re-audit every rendered pair, and keep component colours token-driven so the audit matches the render.
nodes.rationale: Both themes ship and both are audited, so a draft covering one is half a specification. Advisory here by nature — whether a screen was rendered twice is a property of the delivered set, not of any one file, and belongs to a draft-level audit.

nodes.label: The brand accent is for emphasis, never state or primary
nodes.statement: Use the brand accent (--brand, identity #30A1FF) only for emphasis — links, the focus ring, and selection/active indicators. It never replaces the grayscale primary action, is never the sole carrier of state (pair it with text/icon, like any colour), and renders through the APCA-accessible token (--brand: brand-700 on light, brand-300 on dark), never the raw identity hex as text or as a solid fill behind a label.
nodes.rationale: One accent used sparingly reads as brand; the same hue spent on primaries, hover surfaces, or bare state signals dilutes it and reintroduces the inconsistency the grayscale foundation removes.

nodes.label: Build from the library — never hand-roll parallel chrome
nodes.statement: Compose real 2one components. Never hand-roll a parallel sidebar, card, badge, or 'stage' box for something the library already provides.
nodes.rationale: Parallel chrome is the #1 source of inconsistency and responsive/a11y bugs.

nodes.label: Value axes start at zero
nodes.statement: Bar and area charts begin the value axis at zero. A truncated axis is permissible only on a line chart showing rate of change, and only with the truncation labelled.
nodes.rationale: Bar length and area encode magnitude, so a truncated baseline exaggerates differences — the most common way a chart tells a lie its author did not intend. In a draft full of invented data this teaches a false story to everyone who reviews it.

nodes.label: Content pages: header + breadcrumb, not the app menu
nodes.statement: A content/reading page (an explainer, an article) uses a simple header with a clickable logo and a breadcrumb back to the dashboard — not the full app sidebar. Every page has an obvious way home.
nodes.rationale: The app menu on a reading page is noise; a breadcrumb + logo is the clearer, product-standard way back (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §22).

nodes.label: Copy shouldn't lean on the em-dash
nodes.statement: Vary punctuation in visible copy. A view whose sentences repeatedly reach for the em-dash reads as machine-written; prefer commas, colons, periods or parentheses, and keep em-dashes occasional (this rule flags four or more in one view).
nodes.rationale: Em-dash density is the clearest tell of AI-generated prose: models overuse it to an almost comical degree. The fix is a copy pass, not a token, so this rule keeps the voice from drifting back to the default.

nodes.label: Destructive actions confirm + use the destructive variant
nodes.statement: An irreversible action must use the destructive button variant AND require confirmation via AlertDialog before it runs.
nodes.rationale: Undo-less loss demands a deliberate second step and an unmistakable colour.

nodes.label: Destructive styling requires destructive intent
nodes.statement: Reserve destructive styling (the danger colour) for actions that delete or irreversibly change data. Never use destructive styling for ordinary navigation or non-destructive actions.
nodes.rationale: Destructive colour is a warning; spending it on navigation trains users to ignore it and misreads risk.

nodes.label: Empty collections render an Empty state
nodes.statement: A collection with no items renders the Empty component (icon + message + primary next action) — not a blank area.
nodes.rationale: A blank region reads as a bug; an empty state tells the user what to do next.

nodes.label: Form errors are programmatically associated
nodes.statement: A field error must set aria-invalid and link its message with aria-describedby, and show icon+text (see no-color-alone).
nodes.rationale: Screen readers only announce errors that are wired to the control.

nodes.label: Async work has a visible failure path
nodes.statement: Any surface that loads data renders an explicit error state — a message saying what failed and an action to retry. A failed fetch must never leave the loading state up or fall through to the empty state.
nodes.rationale: Loading and empty are the two states everyone draws; error is the one everyone omits, and it is the state the user is most likely to be stuck in. Falling through to "empty" tells them there is no data when in fact the request failed.

nodes.label: Filters offer Select all + Deselect all
nodes.statement: Any multi-select filter (a set of toggleable options that includes/excludes items) must provide Select all and Deselect all (or Clear) controls, so the whole set can be reset in one action instead of toggling every option by hand.
nodes.rationale: Toggling a long filter option-by-option to include everything or start from empty is slow and error-prone; a bulk Select all / Deselect all is the expected, faster affordance and keeps every 2one filter consistent.

nodes.label: Brand marks need a FIXED ground
nodes.statement: Demo the logo on a fixed ground (bg-white / bg-neutral-950), never a theme token. In-app marks must be theme-adaptive (.dark swap or currentColor).
nodes.rationale: The white logo on bg-foreground vanishes in dark (foreground flips near-white).

nodes.label: Visible focus on every interactive element
nodes.statement: Every interactive element must show a clear focus-visible ring (via the --ring token). Never remove the outline without an equal-or-better replacement.
nodes.rationale: Keyboard users navigate by the focus ring; removing it strands them.

nodes.label: Grayscale foundation — one brand accent, no other hues
nodes.statement: Theme the system on a grayscale foundation. Structure and primary actions stay grayscale (near-black on light, white on dark). The only permitted hues are the single brand accent (--brand, identity #30A1FF) for emphasis and the danger/success validation colours — never any other decorative hue.
nodes.rationale: A grayscale foundation with one disciplined accent is what makes every 2one screen read as one system and keeps recolour/theming deterministic; an open palette does not.

nodes.label: No badge stacked directly above a centred hero H1
nodes.statement: Do not open a hero with a pill Badge placed immediately above the H1 in a centred column. That stack is the single most recognisable AI-generated landing-page shape. Integrate the eyebrow into the layout, drop it, or use a left-aligned / asymmetric hero instead.
nodes.rationale: The tells of AI-built design are not ugly, they are generic: the centred hero with a badge on top is the median every model reproduces, and generic is what makes a product forgettable. A design system should read as composed, not defaulted.

nodes.label: Every control defines hover, focus, active and disabled
nodes.statement: A hand-rolled interactive element (a div or span with onClick, a bare <button>) must define hover, focus-visible, active and disabled treatments. Reaching for the library Button instead is always the better answer, because it carries all four already.
nodes.rationale: A draft that shows only the resting state is not a specification — a developer has to invent the other four, which is exactly the drift the system exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Reading a @theme token at runtime? Keep it alive
nodes.statement: Tailwind v4 tree-shakes unused ramp vars. If you read var(--color-<ramp>-<step>) at runtime, safelist the ramp utilities; otherwise prefer the always-live semantic tokens.
nodes.rationale: An un-referenced ramp var is absent from :root and paints blank.

nodes.label: Landing pages lead with the outcome
nodes.statement: A marketing/landing page states what it is and the one thing to do in its H1 and first paragraph (inverted pyramid), before any supporting detail. Headings stand alone out of context in words people search for — no clever or colon ("Topic: subtitle") titles, and no welcome filler.
nodes.rationale: People scan a page before they read it; front-loading the outcome and using literal, standalone headings lets them decide and act without hunting, and matches how search and assistive tech surface a page.

nodes.label: Same destination, same link label
nodes.statement: A given href gets the same accessible name everywhere it repeats — header, footer, and other chrome. The only exception is a genuinely different action to the same URL (e.g. "Start free" vs "Pricing"); document that exception where it occurs.
nodes.rationale: Users who move through repeated chrome (and assistive tech that lists links) rely on a stable name→destination mapping; two labels for one URL, or one label for two, is disorienting (WCAG 2.4.4).

nodes.label: Link text names its destination
nodes.statement: Visible link text must make the destination clear out of its surrounding context. Never use "click here", "read more", "learn more" or a bare "here" as the link, and never show a raw URL as the label — name the destination ("GitHub repository", "live manifest.json"). Links must also be distinguishable by more than colour (an underline or equivalent, with --brand for emphasis), never colour alone.
nodes.rationale: Screen-reader users navigate by a list of links out of context, so "click here" is meaningless and a raw URL is unreadable (WCAG 2.4.4 / Section 508). Colour-only links fail users who can't perceive the hue (WCAG 1.4.1).

nodes.label: Async work shows a loading state
nodes.statement: An async action shows a loading state (Spinner in the trigger; Skeleton for content) and disables re-entry — never a dead click.
nodes.rationale: Silent latency reads as a broken UI and causes double-submits.

nodes.label: Logo: never recolour/rotate/distort
nodes.statement: Never recolour, rotate, stretch, or distort the logo. Use the provided black/white marks on their intended grounds.
nodes.rationale: A modified mark stops being the brand.

nodes.label: Icons: lucide only
nodes.statement: Use lucide-react for every icon. Do not mix a second icon set.
nodes.rationale: One icon library keeps weight, stroke, and metaphor consistent.

nodes.label: Menu toggle shows open vs close
nodes.statement: A toggle-able menu/sidebar shows a hamburger to open and an X (close) when it is open — never the open icon while already open. Reflect the state with aria-expanded and a matching label (Open menu / Close menu).
nodes.rationale: Showing only the open affordance while the menu is open leaves no clear way to close it and misreports state to assistive tech. SidebarTrigger implements this.

nodes.label: Prefer a Sheet over a Dialog on mobile
nodes.statement: On mobile (useIsMobile), present a Dialog's content as a Sheet. Render the trigger at every width; switch the presentation, not the availability.
nodes.rationale: A desktop-sized Dialog is cramped or unreachable on mobile; the Sheet is the reachable equivalent (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §19).

nodes.label: Monospace is for code, not chrome
nodes.statement: Use the mono font only for code blocks and literal commands/paths. Product chrome, labels and prose use the UI font (Inter/Satoshi).
nodes.rationale: Monospace in chrome reads as a developer sampler, not a product, and undercuts the SaaS feel (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §21).

nodes.label: Dark is not invert-and-ship
nodes.statement: Audit every rendered surface×text pair in BOTH themes and keep component colours token-driven so the audit matches the render.
nodes.rationale: A component that hardcodes text-white passes the token audit while rendering unreadable.

nodes.label: No decoration on data marks
nodes.statement: Data marks carry no gradients, drop shadows, 3D or texture. Ink goes to data, not to ornament; grids and axes recede.
nodes.rationale: Decoration on a mark competes with the value it encodes and, with gradients, actively distorts perceived magnitude. Advisory: distinguishing a legitimate area fill from ornament needs judgement a regex does not have.

nodes.label: Never convey state by colour alone
nodes.statement: State (error, success, selected, active) must be carried by an icon and/or text — never colour alone. An invalid field needs an icon plus a message, not just a red border.
nodes.rationale: Colour-only state is invisible to colour-blind and low-vision users; it is a brand AND accessibility rule.

nodes.label: UI counts and lists are generated, not hand-typed
nodes.statement: Any count, badge number, or list shown in the UI derives from the generated source (manifest.json / graph.json) — never a hand-typed literal.
nodes.rationale: Hand-typed numbers drift the moment the repo grows — a nav badge read 198 while the graph held 213. Deriving from source keeps the UI honest by construction (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §20).

nodes.label: Every claim is backed by the repo
nodes.statement: On web copy, state only capabilities, prices, and metrics backed by a repo file, a command, or a human-provided number. Never invent features, commercial terms (billing, annual discounts, checkout), or numbers, and don't collapse the product to one part of it (the knowledge graph is the engine, not the whole product). State honest gaps plainly rather than papering over them.
nodes.rationale: The manifest contract is answer-only-from-repo; marketing copy is where invented claims and fake commercial terms most often creep in, and an unbacked claim is a defect, not a flourish.

nodes.label: One container language — every panel is a real Card
nodes.statement: Every panel is a real Card — same border, radius, padding, shadow. Do not invent bespoke boxes, and do not nest a Card in a Card.
nodes.rationale: One container language is what makes screens feel like one product.

nodes.label: One primary action per view
nodes.statement: Each view/major section has exactly one primary (filled) action. Everything else is outline/ghost/secondary.
nodes.rationale: Competing primaries destroy the visual hierarchy that tells users what to do.

nodes.label: One 8px spacing scale
nodes.statement: Use the 8px spacing scale via Tailwind utilities (gap-4, p-6, mt-6). No ad-hoc inline margins or off-scale pixel values.
nodes.rationale: Inconsistent gaps are the single most visible 'AI-generated' tell.

nodes.label: One system across every surface — even bespoke ones
nodes.statement: Every surface shares the logo, fonts, tokens and theme — including surfaces that cannot be a component shell (e.g. a data-viz canvas). A page that opts out of the shell still opts into the system.
nodes.rationale: A single off-system page (different fonts, no logo, its own palette) breaks the 'one product' feel more than any missing feature (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §23).

nodes.label: Split a product into destination pages
nodes.statement: A product is a set of destination pages (Dashboard, Components, Guide, Graph), not one endless scroll. Keep the global menu short and destination-oriented; deep section lists live on the page, not in the sidebar.
nodes.rationale: One long everything-page is a sampler, not a product — it buries the hierarchy and the way around (docs/building-with-the-dls.md §22).

nodes.label: Buttons are pills (radius-full)
nodes.statement: Buttons use the fully-rounded pill radius — the 2one signature. Do not square them off.
nodes.rationale: The pill is the single most recognisable 2one form cue.

nodes.label: Invented data is visibly marked as placeholder
nodes.statement: Sample content in a draft is labelled as sample — a caption, a watermark, or a banner on the screen. Never present invented figures in a way a reviewer could mistake for real.
nodes.rationale: A draft is made of fake data by definition, and drafts get screenshotted into decks. A plausible invented number that escapes its context becomes a claim nobody meant to make. Advisory here: whether a label reads as a disclaimer is a judgement about the delivered draft, not a property of a file.

nodes.label: All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.statement: Every transition/animation must be disabled or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion. Motion is purposeful (opacity/transform), never decorative.
nodes.rationale: Motion can trigger vestibular disorders; it must be opt-out-able by the OS setting.

nodes.label: Tailwind only keeps classes it can SEE
nodes.statement: @source every folder you render. An arbitrary value (h-[250px]) used in exactly one place is the canary — if it does nothing, the folder was never scanned.
nodes.rationale: A class in an un-scanned folder is never generated at all.

nodes.label: Numbers that are compared are tabular
nodes.statement: Figures in a column, or set side by side for comparison, use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits align.
nodes.rationale: Proportional digits make columns ragged and defeat the comparison the table exists for. The practice is already used in the blocks; without a rule it drifts.

nodes.label: Theme via ThemeProvider — light + audited dark
nodes.statement: Switch themes with the exported ThemeProvider (light + audited dark). Never hand-roll a third palette, a brand hue, or data-* dark hacks.
nodes.rationale: Both shipped themes are APCA-audited; a hand-rolled palette bypasses the audit.

nodes.label: Theme only through tokens — no hard-coded hex or second palette
nodes.statement: Every colour comes from a DLS token. No hard-coded hex, no parallel palette.
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded colour drifts from the tokens and breaks recolour + theming.

nodes.label: Never put essential information only in a Tooltip
nodes.statement: Tooltips are supplementary. Any information the user MUST perceive to succeed (required, error, or instruction) must be visible without hover or focus discovery — not tooltip-only.
nodes.rationale: Tooltips are unreachable on touch and are skipped by many assistive contexts; essential info behind one is lost.

nodes.label: Dates, units and currency are unambiguous
nodes.statement: Write dates as ISO (2026-03-04) or with the month named (4 Mar 2026) — never all-numeric slash form. Always show the unit and the currency.
nodes.rationale: 03/04/2026 is two different days depending on the reader, and a bare number is not a measurement. Draft data is invented, which is exactly when nobody checks the format.

nodes.label: danger/success for state + data trends only
nodes.statement: Use danger and success colours only to express (a) validation state (error/success) and (b) data-trend deltas — growth/decline in metrics, KPIs and data-viz — and in BOTH cases always pair the hue with a direction arrow, icon or text so meaning never rests on colour alone. Never for emphasis, branding, or decoration.
nodes.rationale: Reserving the two hues for state and trend keeps their meaning unambiguous; pairing each with a non-colour cue keeps it accessible (WCAG 1.4.1).

nodes.label: Cap width by content type
nodes.statement: A reading-width cap is for long-form prose only. App/component layouts get a generous responsive cap (max-w-7xl) or go fluid; cap only the prose inside.
nodes.rationale: A reading cap on an app wastes half a large monitor in empty gutters.

nodes.label: Destructive Button
nodes.description: Button variant=destructive — validation/destructive only.

nodes.label: Ghost Button
nodes.description: Button variant=ghost — lowest emphasis.

nodes.label: Link Button
nodes.description: Button variant=link.

nodes.label: Outline Button
nodes.description: Button variant=outline.

nodes.label: Primary Button
nodes.description: Button variant=default — the one solid primary action.

nodes.label: Secondary Button
nodes.description: Button variant=secondary.
